identity.name: Phayao Kingdom
native_names: เมืองพะเยา (Mueang Phayao)

land.text: the throne of Phukamyao, which Chomtham of Ngoenyang took to found a new dynasty at Phayao

predecessors.note: Ngoenyang has no row or dossier. The Phayao page's founding date 'varies by tradition, ranging from 1037 at the earliest to 1131 at the latest'; the Ngoenyang page dates Phayao's secession to 1094 in its infobox, which is inside that range and is used.

land.text: Phayao, annexed by Khamfu in 1338 ('Khamfu then annexed Phayao into Lanna')

successors.note: Cliopatria's Phayao row runs to 1343 and Lan Na's shape grows in 1344.

land.text: the eastern cities of Phayao along the upper Yom basin (read as Pong and Chiang Muan, the Yom headwaters in eastern Phayao; the page names no city)

successors.note: Nan has no Cliopatria row and no dossier; the region is a reading of the Phayao page's 'eastern cities'.

capitals.name: Phayao (Wiang Phayao)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Phayao'. The two capitals, 'later known as Wiang Namtao and Wiang Phayao', are 'now both parts of Phayao city'.

union.text: Thoeng and Chiang Kham, taken by Mangrai in 1261

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1294 core around Phayao plus Thoeng and Chiang Kham (before the 1261 campaign)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1094-1260. The Ngoenyang infobox dates Phayao's secession to 1094 (the Phayao page puts the founding between 1037 and 1131) and the core is at Phayao; Cliopatria starts in 1294. Before 1261 the kingdom also held Thoeng and Chiang Kham, which Mangrai annexed ('annexed Thoeng and Chiang Kham (1261 campaign)'); Cliopatria's 4,552-km2 shape (18 cells) is the remainder. The page's own description of the extent is the whole Yonok basin ('the Ing, Kok, Wang, Yom, Nan and Khop river basins', parts of Chiang Rai, Phayao, Lampang, Phrae and Nan), a much larger and vaguer area than the shape; unverified.

Years only: 1294-1332 (and the 1261 shape above for earlier years). 5,231 km2 (18 cells, 99.97-100.66 E, 18.96-19.59 N): the Phayao core after Mangrai's annexations. The Mangrai page counts 'Thoeng (taken from Phayao)' in his realm at his death. The Phayao page gives no area.

Years only: 1333-1337. The shape is unchanged from 1294 (18 cells). The page dates the annexation to 1338, not Cliopatria's 1343/1344: 'In 1338, Khamfu ... invited Phaya Phanong of Nan Kingdom to attack Phayao.'

region.text: Phukamyao, the Phayao basin around Wiang Phayao and Wiang Namtao

ledger.note: 1094: Phayao separates from Ngoenyang under Chomtham's dynasty. The Ngoenyang page: 'Phayao's secession is dated to 1094 in the infobox'; the Phayao page: 'Founding date varies by tradition, ranging from 1037 at the earliest to 1131 at the latest' and Chomtham was sent 'to take empty throne of Phukamyao'. Neither gives a boundary.

region.text: Thoeng and Chiang Kham, taken by Mangrai after his accession in 1261 (undated)

ledger.note: Bridge at 1261: Mangrai's Ngoenyang annexes Thoeng and Chiang Kham. Phayao page: 'Mangrai annexed the city of Thoeng and Chiang Kham from the Phayao kingdom' (undated; its 1261 is the accession: 'When Mangrai ascended to the throne of Ngoenyang in 1261'); Mangrai page: 'conquering Chiang Kham and Thoeng, which belonged to the Phayao kingdom' (undated). Phan and Chiang Khian were ceded to Ngoenyang and returned in 1296 (undated cession; not drawn, below the grid). Confidence lowered from 2 by the se-01-d reviewer: neither page dates the annexation.

region.text: Phayao, minus the eastern cities that went to Nan

ledger.note: 1338: Khamfu of Chiang Saen annexes Phayao into Lan Na. 'In 1338, Khamfu, the son of Saenphu ... invited Phaya Phanong of Nan Kingdom to attack Phayao. Khamfu then annexed Phayao into Lanna.'

region.text: the eastern cities of Phayao along the upper Yom basin (read as Pong and Chiang Muan, the Yom headwaters in eastern Phayao; the page names no city)

ledger.note: 1338: the eastern cities go to Nan. Phayao page: 'the eastern cities of Phayao along the upper Yom basin was annexed into Nan'. The page names no city; the region is the Yom headwaters inside Phayao (Pong, Chiang Muan). Region corrected by the se-01-d reviewer: it was Phrae province, which lies outside Phayao's shape and was not 'of Phayao'; counterpart slug was 'Nan'.
1338: the Phayao Kingdom ends. Infobox: last ruler Khamlue, 1338, annexed by Lan Na. Cliopatria's row runs to 1343.

wars.name: Mangrai's Phayao campaign of 1261

zones.text: Thoeng and Chiang Kham, taken by Mangrai in 1261

wars.outcome: Mangrai annexed Thoeng and Chiang Kham.
wars.note: Mangrai later made peace between Ngammueang of Phayao and Ramkhamhaeng of Sukhothai (the Three Kings Alliance, Mangrai page: 1287; the Phayao page gives no date).

wars.name: Khamfu's annexation of Phayao
wars.outcome: Phayao annexed into Lan Na, its eastern cities into Nan.
wars.note: The Lan Na page's text gives 1456 (Tilokaraj), against its own infobox and the Phayao page.

certainty.note: A mueang of the Yonok basin; no page gives a frontier.

notes:
Cliopatria begins the Phayao row in 1294 and ends it in 1343; the pages put the annexation in 1338 and the founding between 1037 and 1131. The start 1094 (Ngoenyang infobox; the Phayao page gives only the range 1037-1131) and the keyframe 1094-1260 are bridges: Cliopatria's core with Thoeng and Chiang Kham added back. The page's description of the extent (the whole Yonok basin) is much larger than Cliopatria's 18 cells and is not drawn.
Page budget (1-2 pages) met with the Phayao page and the Mangrai page, plus the Lan Na and Ngoenyang pages opened for the Lan Na dossier. No area on any page. Disagreements: Ngammueang's accession 1258 (text) against 1261 (infobox); Phayao's end 1338 (Phayao page, Lan Na infobox) against 1456 (Lan Na text) and Cliopatria's 1343; the Three Kings Alliance has no date on the Phayao page (1287 on the Mangrai page).
Counterparts without dossiers: ngoenyang (the predecessor; infobox foundation 638, Mangrai's accession 1261/1262, Foundation of Lanna 1292) and Nan (the Kingdom of Nan, which received the eastern cities in 1338): both need dossiers from the additions batch. Gazetteer: Thoeng and Chiang Kham are not places in the gazetteer (radius used).
